replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I haven't used AI for math learning recently. My focus is on hobbies and reading novels. I find AI tools too technical and prefer hands-on problem-solving through real-world examples rather than digital interfaces.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: Start by writing the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points are where the slope is zero, indicating local maxima or minima.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data dimensions by finding directions of maximum variance. It involves standardizing data, computing the covariance matrix, finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and projecting data onto the new axes. The math is manageable with basic linear algebra; don't worry—start with simple datasets.
